source.title: Cardiac vagal control in response to acute stress during pregnancy: Associations with life stress and emotional support.

confidence_rationale: Directly relevant double-edged anchor: it (i) confirms vagal rebound (HRV recovery) as a discrete, separately-modelled recovery axis via piecewise growth-curve modelling of reactivity vs recovery slopes, AND (ii) shows emotional support modulates the rebound. For the candidate (endogenous, NON-social rebound) this is 'mixed': it validates the shared recovery variable and its dissociability from reactivity, but its experimental lever is social support -- which is the MECH-355 soothing side, not the endogenous trigger. That is exactly why it supports the ARCHITECTURE (sibling claims sharing one recovery target via distinct triggers) while not isolating the endogenous trigger.
failure_signatures: Greater vagal rebound was evident ONLY for women reporting high emotional support -- demonstrating that a social input can be the proximate modulator of rebound, so an endogenous-rebound experiment must hold social inputs fixed/absent to isolate the offset-triggered component (confound between MECH-355 and the sibling if not controlled).

Higher life stress predicted both greater reactivity AND faster vagal rebound (adaptation to anticipated high-stress environments) -- rebound magnitude is history-dependent, so a fixed-rate REE rebound would mis-model chronically-stressed agents.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In pregnant women, piecewise growth-curve modelling separated reactivity and recovery slopes of HRV (RMSSD) across the Trier Social Stress Test; life stress predicted greater HRV reactivity and greater HRV recovery (vagal rebound), but the rebound association held only among women reporting high emotional support.
mapping.ree_translation: Vagal rebound is a separately-modellable recovery axis (distinct slope from reactivity) -- supporting that an endogenous-recovery mechanism is a real, isolable target -- AND a social input (emotional support) modulates that same recovery axis. In REE this is the precise warrant for the design-pass architecture: register the endogenous, offset-triggered rebound as a SIBLING of MECH-355 soothing that shares the recovery target (MECH-219 recovery_rate / SD-032e drive_bias leak) but is driven by an internal offset signal rather than a conspecific. The two inputs converge on one variable; they are dissociable by trigger, not by effector.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The experimental manipulation here is SOCIAL (emotional support), so the paper most directly evidences the MECH-355 soothing input; it supports the endogenous-rebound claim only at the level of 'rebound is a discrete recovery axis that multiple inputs can drive'. It does not isolate an endogenous, non-social trigger. Pregnant-women sample + TSST; transfer to a non-social REE agent is by analogy on the shared-recovery-variable structure.
mapping.source_context: 191 pregnant women (predominantly Black, urban, high public-assistance); Trier Social Stress Test; HR and RMSSD across preparation/task/recovery; piecewise growth-curve modelling of reactivity and recovery slopes.

confidence_components.notes: Well-powered, modern modelling that explicitly separates recovery from reactivity slopes -- strong on the 'recovery is its own axis' point. Direction is mixed because its lever is social support (MECH-355 side); it evidences the sibling architecture more than the endogenous trigger per se.
